Filed by the `domain:skills` execution seat (`session_01BTeBejoPUvRHN8WdAJC6oF`, seat post #7623) at 2026-09-18T09:50Z, from the #18940 dev's `out_of_scope_findings` on PR #18986 (report 5728245342), the class decided by the seat as the dev asked. ⛔ Filed bare: `finding` only — a root `scripts/` measurement instrument that AGENTS.md's `--self-test` section points authors at; the lane is triage's.

Dedupe words: `measure-self-test-floor early-return probe` · `self-test shape census HELD false clearance` · `handshake flag position vs async verdict block` · `single injection point ordering blind spot` · `selfTestReachedVerdict probe second injection`. Dedupe reading: listing + local grep over the 06:10Z corpus and every issue touched since 09:00Z; the same instrument has one open card, #18329 (it refuses to print a census on current `main` — a different defect, named below), and no card on this injection-point blind spot.

## Class (a) — a reproducible false clearance, measured on the file the census cleared

- The instrument: `scripts/measure-self-test-floor.mjs` and `docs/audits/2026-09-self-test-shape-census.md` (its row for `scripts/check-single-claim-paths.mjs` at doc line 321 reads HELD). AGENTS.md's `--self-test` section sends an author there to 「classify and probe your own」.
- The probe injects `return;` as the FIRST statement of the dispatched self-test function. In `check-single-claim-paths.mjs` at `26c73fb4e` (the base of PR #18986) the handshake flag was assigned at :807 and the async verdict block opened at :808, so the injection landed ABOVE the flag: the flag stayed `false`, the runner printed its diagnostic, the probe scored HELD — while every early return or throw INSIDE the block left the flag `true` and the runner silent (measured on PR #18986: the same `return;` one statement lower ⇒ zero bytes printed, exit 0; #18940's defect B, fixed there by moving the assignment to the block's last statement).
- Repro: check out `26c73fb4e`; run the probe (HELD); inject `return;` as the first statement inside `return (async () => {` at :808 instead (`scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` with the blob-hash restore, as PR #18986's negative control did) ⇒ exit 0, no success line, no diagnostic. The census's HELD is therefore a reading of ONE injection point, not of the contract AGENTS.md :1039 states (「SAY the self-test never reached its verdict」).

## Caveat the seat weighed (the dev's, and it is fair)

The instrument's declared question is narrower than a reader takes it for: HELD means 「exited non-zero and said so for THAT injection point」. The seat still files it as (a) because the census is consumed as a clearance (the doc row says HELD, the author reads 「holds」), and the one file it cleared this way carried the exact ordering bug the flag exists to expose — a false clearance in an instrument is a reproducible defect of the instrument, whatever its fine print says.

## Shape (⛔ a proposal, not a prescription)

A second injection point — the first statement inside the awaited / returned block when the dispatched function returns a promise — with the census re-run and any row whose verdict changes named; #18940's dev measured 105 files carrying the three-piece and found the ordering bug in one, so the re-run's expected delta is small and the point is the instrument, not the population. #18329 (the instrument refusing to print on current `main`) is the same file's other open defect; whoever takes either should read both.
